title: VPAT evidence pack + keyboard/focus polish for interactive data components
creator: Ava Chen
description: Consolidate accessibility fixes and artifacts needed to complete a VPAT (Voluntary Product Accessibility Template) submission focused on dense data surfaces: tables, compact lists, interactive charts (SVG/canvas), and system buttons/token usage. This ticket covers: mapping current token contrast deltas, establishing keyboard focus/roving focus patterns for table rows and chart elements, ARIA attribute audit and pragmatic remediation for complex widgets, and producing the VPAT evidence pack (screenshots, code samples, keyboard walkthrough scripts). The goal is to unblock compliance review and provide clear, designer/engineer playbooks for consistent implementation across the component library.
acceptance_criteria: VPAT spreadsheet has entries for each affected component with pass/fail + remediation notes
Contrast issues reduced: all tokens used in table cells, buttons, and chart labels meet WCAG AA (4.5:1) for normal text or provide justification in VPAT if lower for visual-cue-only elements

Keyboard navigation: table row focus + keyboard selection works with Arrow/Enter/Escape; charts allow keyboard focus on interactive marks and keyboard-triggered tooltips; documented in component READMEs
ARIA: role/aria-* coverage implemented for row/group semantics, live regions for tooltip announcements, and examples for screen reader interaction patterns
Design tokens: mapping document (old token -> accessible token) committed and PR opened linking to token changes
QA checklist and automated a11y test harness (axe/core or Lighthouse scripts) added to component stories where applicable
VPAT evidence bundle (screenshots, step-by-step keyboard script, code snippets) uploaded to Confluence and linked in the ticket
comments: 2026-03-02 - Ava Chen: Kickoff notes — Confirmed scope with PM (Marisol). Prioritized tables, dense list items, and interactive chart marks. Decided to treat chart axes/labels as text for contrast checks and interactive marks as controls requiring focus styles.

2026-03-04 - Liam Patel: Did initial token sweep. Found three low-contrast uses: token.control-muted (used in compact table subtext), token.chart-label (used on dark backgrounds), token.icon-secondary (used in tiny inline action buttons). Patch planned to introduce token.accessible-muted and token.chart-label-contrast. Linking token PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-tokens/pull/342

2026-03-05 - Accessibility review (external consultant): Recommended roving tabindex pattern for table keyboard nav instead of focusing row-level buttons to reduce tab stops. Also advised announcing chart focus changes using aria-live polite. Attached consultant notes to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/VX-1234

2026-03-06 - Liam Patel: Engineering spike complete. Prototype for table keyboard nav implemented in storybook: /stories/table/a11y-roving-focus. Implementation uses data-row-index and a11y util (keyboardRover) with ArrowUp/ArrowDown and Space/Enter handlers. Opening PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/1219

2026-03-07 - Designer review (Ava Chen): Requested that focus ring color use token.focus-critical for high contrast instead of the current 2px semi-transparent outline. Also flagged that dense rows need slightly larger hit targets — proposed small padding bump + token.token-dense-hit to 6px min.

2026-03-08 - QA (Jamal Ortega): Ran axe on modified stories. Two remaining violations: contrast failure for chart label on gradient background (needs token swap) and missing aria-describedby for complex cell tooltips. Added sub-issues: DES-126544 and DES-126545. Marking this ticket to depend on DES-126544.

2026-03-09 - Liam Patel: Updated PR with focus style changes and added unit tests for keyboard rover behavior. Screenshots (keyboard navigation walkthrough) uploaded to Confluence page. PR link updated in this ticket.

2026-03-10 - Ava Chen: Drafted VPAT entries for Tables and Charts sections; left justification notes where visual contrast choices are design-led (e.g., color-coded sparkline meaning). Need engineering confirmation on runtime aria-live behavior before finalizing VPAT. TODO: schedule review with Compliance next week.
